pipeline_validation.note: Scores are low (REJECT-range) because search-provider results carry no jd_text -- an honest consequence of not fabricating a job description, not a scoring engine defect. score_job.py itself was not modified.

deliberate_design_choices: Manual import is a human-typed/pasted FORM, not a server-side URL fetch -- avoids any ambiguity around whether a single agent-triggered fetch of a restricted site counts as 'automated means' under that site's own robots.txt language.

A manually-imported job's `source`/`job_source` is the real platform name (e.g. LINKEDIN), not a synthetic label -- so it shares job_id identity with any future real adapter for that platform and dedupes naturally; `discovery_source=MANUAL_IMPORT` preserves how it was actually found.

web_search_evidence_capture.py is a one-time, agent-supervised evidence artifact, never imported by api/main.py or wired into the running backend -- the backend's WEB_SEARCH_BACKEND remains None, exactly as honestly documented before this phase.

No existing saved-search 'sources' checkbox list was extended to include LinkedIn/Indeed/etc., since search_store.validate_sources() only accepts AdapterStatus.ENABLED sources and those seven are not -- adding them as checkboxes that silently discover nothing would violate the project's 'never pretend' rule. Manual import is surfaced instead, with an explicit note in the New Search UI naming which sources it will not include.
